title: A Smooth Metric with No Local Isometric Immersion into Three-Space
sections_read: model patch and Darboux height equation
all cap regularity proof and weighted multiplier estimate
all oscillatory pulse, propagation, Taylor comparison and Baire argument
all smooth assembly, boundary obstruction and flat-jet corollary
four figure sources and complete bibliography
claim_as_stated: The manuscript claims a smooth positive metric, flat to all orders relative to the Euclidean metric at the origin, admitting no smooth local isometric immersion into R3 near the origin. Its curvature changes sign; it does not settle either fixed curvature-sign case.
proof_architecture: Use only the necessary Darboux equation for a fixed ambient height; define a whole-square class with E>0, nonzero diagonal Hessian and small mixed-to-diagonal ratio.

Differentiate before changing to solution-dependent flow coordinates. Curvature commutation contributes a drift; combine directed weights near negative/zero curvature with a weighted elliptic estimate elsewhere to gain derivatives without high-order data on the artificial cap edge.

Under hypothetical density of a bounded height class, perturb the metric itself in a thin oscillatory strip. Propagate cap data to both strip edges and construct a finite Taylor comparison for the unperturbed metric.

Pair forcing with the same oscillatory test. Its constant-sign moment is linear in fixed width parameter delta, whereas leading competing terms are quadratic. Fix delta before frequency tau tends to infinity; Baire category excludes all countably bounded classes.

Place disjoint obstructed patches, in every orientation from a finite net, accumulating around negative disks; let the disks accumulate at the origin. Choose amplitudes stagewise small in every previously listed derivative seminorm.

A hypothetical local graph immersion has a nonzero rank-one second fundamental form at a disk boundary point. A nearby full patch aligned to its kernel supplies an admissible height forbidden by the patch construction. The summed metric keeps all Euclidean jets at the origin.

construction_ideas.mechanism: Two-scale contradiction with shared leading order
construction_ideas.premises: A forcing moment bounded below by c delta times a common scale, and competing cost bounded above by C delta^2 at that same scale, with c,C independent of sufficiently small fixed delta.
construction_ideas.possible_interface: Search for a determinant normalization whose desired gain is first order and paid cross-errors are second order in a separately fixed parameter, before sending H or denominator to infinity.
construction_ideas.missing_bridge: No such determinant estimates have been constructed; the existing fixed analytic cost cannot be discarded or treated as quadratic.

construction_ideas.mechanism: Countable local obstructions assembled while preserving every finite regularity requirement
construction_ideas.premises: Disjoint supports, perturbations arbitrarily small in finitely many C^m seminorms, and summable tails for each fixed derivative order.
construction_ideas.possible_interface: A prototype for preserving earlier finite certificates while adding infinitely many new obstructions or witnesses. Explicitly pay the lambda^(-m-2) rescaling cost at each stage.
construction_ideas.missing_bridge: Integer coefficients and denominator heights do not admit freely chosen tiny smooth perturbations. C-infinity flat bump freedom also does not hold for the analytic digit-transport functions used in the pi project.

construction_ideas.mechanism: Finite orientation net captures an unknown rank-one witness
construction_ideas.premises: A genuinely nonzero rank-one form, strict inequalities stable in a neighborhood, and patches at every boundary point in every net direction.
construction_ideas.possible_interface: Try replacing selection of one unknown pivot/witness by finitely many robust direction tests, while retaining all tests in later extensions.
construction_ideas.missing_bridge: The rank gap and stability radius may degenerate with matrix height; no H-uniform net or arithmetic height bound is supplied.

limits: First-pass source reading, not independent verification of cap estimates or main theorem.
Referenced external PDE and geometric literature was not independently reread here.
The source itself reports an unresolved discrepancy between an earlier preprint and later accounts of the smooth local-realizability problem.
Smooth flatness at a point is not an analytic flatness construction and cannot be transplanted into a fixed integer digit sequence.
